tags.gist: Proposes concordance behavior, how far the user's assertions can move a device's view of them, as a named risk dimension dominant in mental health.
Says concordance is a compounding trajectory property; multi-turn evaluation should use adversarial trajectories where a simulated user minimizes and asks the device to stand down.
Describes its own system letting the risk estimate rise readily on deterioration but fall slowly on reassurance, built into the computation rather than prompted.
Says the two escalation errors differ in kind in suicide-risk settings, cautions against netting them, and wants separate rates justified per deployment population.
Observes the severity of over-escalation depends on architecture: offering contact leaves the decision human, while initiating contact carries the full false-positive weight.
Wants benchmarking to ask whether a safety behavior is enforced by a component the model can influence, since instructions can be overridden, execution paths cannot.
Supports traceability and proposes checking a device's statements about the patient against a closed, enumerated record before display as a premarket-evaluable property.
Suggests corpus closure may merit its own premarket risk characteristic, since open-retrieval devices cannot have patient assertions verified.
Proposes device-generated integrity metrics, such as the rate of unverifiable assertions, as a fourth approach and a continuous, early trigger for re-benchmarking.
Says a supervisor is only as reliable as its ground-truth definition; its own narrow roster nearly flagged a true, vital statement as fabricated.
Wants supervisor evaluation to show known-true assertions pass unaltered, since false positives that suppress truth look like normal operation.
Suggests supervisors run in observation-only mode, recording but not altering output, before gaining authority, as a general expectation.
Wants the supervisor's corpus definition treated as an explicitly reviewable artifact, since that is where its errors live.
Says monitoring that relies on machine supervision should earn no premarket credit until the supervisor's reliability is separately shown, or uncertainty merely moves.
As a self-funded developer, warns that obligations scaled to large firms select for size; automated metrics are feasible, mandatory paid third-party review is not.
Asks the framework to distinguish devices where the AI is the endpoint from devices built to bring a human in, a built-in downstream safeguard.
Describes its system preparing and offering contact, including a crisis line, but never placing calls, so an autonomous action becomes an offered one.
Warns a framework blind to the endpoint-versus-bridge distinction will over-regulate the safer design or under-regulate the other.
Raises behavior when connectivity is degraded or absent: for safety-critical functions, evaluation should cover offline behavior and what the device tells users about reduced capability.
Notes its offline architecture is designed but mostly unbuilt, saying regulators must be able to rely on the built-versus-designed distinction.
